Conquest of Canaan
KON-kwest uhv KAY-nuhn
noun
From conquest + Canaan; the taking of the promised land by Israel under Joshua.

Biblical Definition

The conquest of Canaan is the taking of the promised land by Israel under Joshua, after the forty years in the wilderness, in fulfilment of the oath the LORD sware to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Israel crossed Jordan on dry ground as the priests bare the ark, took Jericho when its walls fell at the trumpet and the shout, and, after the sin of Achan was purged, went on to subdue the kings of the south and the north, until Joshua took the whole land according to all that the LORD said unto Moses. The conquest was the LORD’s war and the LORD’s gift: He fought for Israel, drove out the nations before them, and gave them a land for which they did not labour, cities they built not, and vineyards they planted not. It was also an act of righteous judgment upon the Canaanite nations, whose iniquity was now full—a people given over to idolatry, child sacrifice, and abominations, whom the LORD cast out before His people, that Israel might not learn their ways. The dictionary honors the conquest of Canaan as the fulfilment of covenant promise, the gift of rest to the people of God, and the righteous judgment of the LORD upon a ripened wickedness—a foreshadowing of the rest that remaineth for the people of God and of the final judgment by which the Lord shall give His saints their inheritance and cast out the wicked for ever.

Webster 1828 Definition

The taking of the promised land by Israel under Joshua; the LORD’s war and gift in fulfilment of the covenant, and His righteous judgment on ripened Canaanite wickedness.

CONQUEST OF CANAAN, Israel’s taking of the promised land under Joshua.

Israel crossed Jordan on dry ground behind the ark.

Jericho fell at the trumpet and the shout; Achan’s sin was purged.

Joshua subdued the kings of the south and the north.

The LORD’s war, His covenant gift, and His judgment on ripened sin.

Key Scripture

Jos 21:45 — "There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass."

Jos 11:23 — "So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD said unto Moses; and Joshua gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land rested from war."

Deu 9:5 — "Not for thy righteousness, or for the uprightness of thine heart, dost thou go to possess their land: but for the wickedness of these nations the LORD thy God doth drive them out from before thee, and that he may perform the word which the LORD sware unto thy fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."

Jos 24:13 — "And I have given you a land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat."

Modern Corruption

The conquest is condemned as genocide by modern moral judgment, or spiritualized away; Scripture presents it as covenant fulfilment and righteous judgment on ripened sin.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition beyond the moral objection. The chief corruption is the modern charge that the conquest was genocide, an atrocity to be condemned by the conscience of a later age. This judgment sets fallen man as judge over God and forgets two truths Scripture presses. First, the LORD is the Judge of all the earth, and the conquest was His righteous judgment upon nations whose iniquity was full (Gen 15:16)—a people given to idolatry, child sacrifice, and abomination, cast out for their own wickedness, not for Israel’s righteousness (Deu 9:5).

Second, the conquest was the fulfilment of covenant promise and the gift of rest. The LORD gave Israel a land for which they did not labour, cities they built not (Jos 24:13), and not one good thing failed of all He had spoken (Jos 21:45). To spiritualize the conquest away, on the other hand, empties it of its historical reality and its place in redemption. The dictionary holds both: the conquest was real history, righteous judgment on ripened sin, and covenant gift—a foreshadowing of the rest that remaineth for the people of God and of the last judgment, when the Lord shall give His saints their inheritance and cast out the wicked for ever.
